current_exact_evidence.interpretation: FLEURS fixture materialized as IEEE-float WAV while the admitted comparator validation path requires mono 16 kHz 16-bit PCM. Failure occurred before Nemotron ASR quality/latency could be measured.

primary_source_findings.finding: Python 3.13 wave supports uncompressed PCM WAV; IEEE-float WAV is outside that admitted reader capability.
Python 3.15 adds IEEE floating-point WAV support, proving that accepting format tag 3 is Python-runtime-version-sensitive rather than a stable comparator invariant across earlier runtimes.
FLEURS exposes audio arrays as float32 with sampling_rate 16000; fixture serialization must therefore bind its own deterministic encoding rather than assume PCM16 from the decoded array.
python-soundfile supports explicit WAV subtypes and documents PCM_16 as the default WAV subtype; using an explicit PCM_16 subtype makes the fixture contract auditable.

hypothesis_fusion.H1: The present blocker is fixture-envelope validity, not Nemotron ASR behavior.
hypothesis_fusion.H2: Upgrading Python to gain float-WAV support would unnecessarily change runtime environment semantics and weaken exact-subject comparability.
hypothesis_fusion.H3: Deterministic normalization of the already pinned FLEURS samples to mono 16 kHz PCM_16, with source and normalized digests, is the smallest high-information repair that preserves model/corpus/gate/right-context axes.
hypothesis_fusion.counterhypothesis: The normalized fixture may still reveal a later independent comparator, model-load, receipt-contract, or ASR product failure; no such result may be inferred before execution.
hypothesis_fusion.decision: Preserve the F2-required fixture-only repair and do not open a new model or architecture lane.
